paper_information.title: Climate Smart Technologies and Practices for Increasing the Soybean Productivity
paper_information.journal_or_source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research & National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE)
paper_information.abstract_summary: This e-book is a compilation of resource texts on climate smart technologies and practices for increasing soybean production and productivity, covering varieties, agronomic practices, nutrition, weed, pest and disease management, abiotic stress management, and mechanization.
paper_information.research_objective: To educate extension workers, students, research scholars, and academicians on climate smart technologies and practices for increasing soybean production and productivity in response to changing climate scenarios.
important_findings: Average soybean productivity in India is stagnated around 1 ton/ha compared to world average of 2.3 t/ha.
Improved technologies and practices under AICRP on Soybean can achieve productivity levels of more than 2.5 ton/ha.
Integrated crop management, balanced nutrition, use of climate-smart varieties, and proper water/tillage management can significantly mitigate climate change risks.
